title: Quarter boundary synchronization and initiative ownership roster
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Company-level OKRs are not consistently translated into clear quarter boundaries and single-party initiative owners; cross-team dependencies are discovered late and derail delivery.

Objectives: 1) Define a lightweight Quarter Boundary Synchronization protocol (QBS) to lock objectives, owners, and primary dependencies 3 weeks before sprint planning. 2) Publish an Initiative Ownership Roster (IOR) listing single-point owners, backup owners, decision authority, and escalation contacts for each company-level initiative. 3) Pilot the protocol across Product, Eng, Design, and Research for Q2 planning and capture metrics to iterate.

Why now: Growth of Dedicated and Private product lines increased cross-team coupling; incidents and rollout delays in past two quarters traced to unclear ownership and last-minute scope changes.

Deliverables: 1) QBS doc (one-pager + template) in Confluence. 2) IOR spreadsheet and vanity view in the Roadmap dashboard. 3) Runbook for escalation and a small decision ledger template. 4) Pilot retrofit for 6 highest-risk initiatives.

Acceptance criteria: - QBS doc ratified by PM leadership and Design and Eng leads. - IOR populated for top 20 initiatives with owner, backup, decision authority, and escalation contact. - Pilot shows a 30% reduction in cross-team dependency Slack threads during planning windows vs previous quarter (measured in roadmap-dashboard). - At least two canary initiatives complete end-to-end using the QBS and decision ledger with documented learnings.
updates: 2025-01-12: Kickoff meeting with PM, Eng, Design. Agreed scope: company-level initiatives only; exclude minor backlog tickets.
2025-01-18: Draft of QBS one-pager created (Confluence) and shared with stakeholders for feedback. Link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OKR/QBS+Draft
2025-01-22: Design provided initial IOR schema (owner, backup, decision authority, escalation path, SLAs). DES review notes: reduce columns to reduce maintenance burden.
2025-01-28: Engineering flagged two infra initiatives (ENG-1842, ENG-1907) with hard dependencies; added to dependencies list and scheduled deep-dive on 2025-02-02.
2025-02-02: Deep-dive with Eng leads; decision: lock interface contract doc and add automatic notification to roadmap dashboard when a dependency status changes.
2025-02-06: Pilot roster populated for 6 initiatives; assigned single-point owners and backups. Sent to execs for signoff.
2025-02-10: PM leadership asked to add an explicit 'decision authority' column to IOR; updated template and created Decision Ledger starter PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/roadmap/pull/72
2025-02-12: Status: In Progress. Next: finalize Confluence QBS page, wire IOR into roadmap dashboard, schedule pilot retro on 2025-03-10.
risks: R1: Owners may not keep roster updated — mitigations: automated calendar reminders and badge on roadmap dashboard showing last-updated date.
R2: Org changes during quarter shift authority — mitigations: require owner to nominate backup and decision authority; include org-change clause in IOR template.
R3: Tooling integration takes longer than QBS timeline — mitigation: fall back to lightweight spreadsheet and email digest while integrations finish.
metrics: M1: % of company-level initiatives with single-point owner by T-21 days (target 95%)
M2: # of cross-team dependency Slack threads during planning window (target -30% vs baseline)
M3: Time from dependency discovery to resolution (target median < 7 days)
M4: Roster freshness (median days since last update, target < 14 days)
